title: Jensen Huang on Rogan: surviving Nvidia's near-death, fear as fuel, and why AI won't end jobs
summary: Jensen tells Nvidia's origin story: an impossible 1993 mission, three wrong technology bets, Sega's $5M lifeline, and an untested chip tape-out. He explains leading through vulnerability, first-principles reassessment and fear of failure, and why AI, energy and jobs will change gradually.

principles.text: Fear of failure drives him more than the desire to succeed.
principles.quote: I have a greater drive from not wanting to fail than the drive of wanting to succeed.

principles.text: Vulnerable leaders can pivot; leaders who must always be right cannot.
principles.quote: the more vulnerable we are as a leader the more able other people are able to tell you you know that Jensen that's not exactly right

principles.text: Reason from first principles and reassess continuously, even though it breeds anxiety.
principles.quote: I just have to make sure that I stay alert, that I reason about things from first principles all the time. Always break things down to first principles.

principles.text: Crisis teaches you to strip waste and do only what is essential.
principles.quote: We learned how to remove all waste in the company and work from first principles and doing only the things that are essential.

principles.text: Narrow focus on one audience, plus an ecosystem, turns technology into a platform.
principles.quote: instead of building a 3D graphics chip for every 3D graphics application, we decided to build a 3D graphics chip for one application. We bet the farm on video games.

principles.text: Success involves long suffering, and sharing that honestly helps others.
principles.quote: there's long periods of suffering and loneliness and uncertainty and fear and embarrassment and humiliation.
